title: Ligaments, capsule and rotator cuff of the shoulder (anterior)
lab: Shoulder Joint, Scapular Muscles, and Posterior Arm
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Acromion of the scapula to the lateral end of the clavicle, across the top of the joint between them.
Strengthens the acromioclavicular joint and resists forward and backward sliding of the clavicle.
hy: A fall onto the point of the shoulder separates the acromioclavicular joint. This ligament tears first; when the coracoclavicular ligament tears too, the clavicle rides up.

rows: Coracoid process to the acromion, both parts of the scapula.
With the acromion and the coracoid process it forms an arch over the head of the humerus that stops it from being pushed upward.
hy: The supraspinatus tendon and the subacromial bursa can be pinched under this arch when the arm is raised (shoulder impingement).

rows: Upper surface of the coracoid process to the trapezoid line on the underside of the clavicle. It is the lateral part of the coracoclavicular ligament.
With the conoid ligament it hangs the scapula from the clavicle. It stops the acromion from being driven under the clavicle.
Base of the coracoid process to the conoid tubercle on the underside of the clavicle. It is the medial part of the coracoclavicular ligament.
With the trapezoid ligament it hangs the scapula and the upper limb from the clavicle and keeps the clavicle from riding upward.
Greater tubercle to lesser tubercle of the humerus, bridging the intertubercular sulcus.
Holds the tendon of the long head of biceps brachii in the sulcus.

structures.name: Joint capsule of the shoulder (glenohumeral joint)
prompts: Joint capsule of the shoulder (glenohumeral joint)

rows: Margin of the glenoid cavity to the anatomical neck of the humerus.
Encloses the shoulder joint. It is loose, especially below, which allows the wide range of movement; the glenohumeral ligaments and the rotator cuff tendons strengthen it.
hy: The lower part of the capsule has no rotator cuff support, so the head of the humerus most often dislocates anteriorly and inferiorly. The axillary nerve is at risk.

rows: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus.

Starts abduction of the arm, where it is the main abductor for about the first 15 degrees, and then helps the deltoid through the rest of the movement. Holds the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.
hy: The most often injured rotator cuff muscle: its tendon is pinched under the acromion. Tested with the empty can (Jobe) test.
Rotator cuff muscles, SItS: Supraspinatus, Infraspinatus, teres minor, Subscapularis.

rows: Subscapular fossa on the anterior surface of the scapula.
Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5, C6).
Medially rotates the arm. With the other rotator cuff muscles it holds the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.
